notes.summary: Venn diagram questions ask you to pick the diagram that best shows the relation between three groups, or to read numbers from a given diagram. About 1 question per paper.

concepts.title: Three basic relations
concepts.body:
Inside: every A is a B (Dog inside Animal).
Overlap: some A are B (Women and Doctors).
Separate: no A is B (Cat and Dog).

concepts.title: Check every pair
concepts.body: With three items, decide the relation for each of the three pairs (A–B, B–C, A–C), then find the diagram that shows all three correctly.

concepts.title: Reading a numbered diagram
concepts.body: A number inside only one circle belongs to that group only. A number in the overlap of two circles belongs to both. "Exactly two" means overlaps of two circles, not the centre.

varieties.name: Best representing diagram
varieties.how: Decide inside / overlap / separate for every pair, then match the picture.

steps: Dog inside Animal; Cat inside Animal.
example.answer: One big circle with two separate circles inside

varieties.name: Numbers in a diagram
varieties.how: Mark the regions asked for and add only those numbers.

example.q: In the figure, how many people are singers and dancers but not actors?
steps: Overlap of Singers and Dancers only, outside Actors.

tips: Write the relation of each pair before looking at the options.
In counting questions, shade the required region with your finger first.
traps: "Some" items overlap; do not draw one inside the other unless "all" is true.
"Exactly two groups" excludes the centre region (all three).

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship between Mothers, Women and Doctors?
questions.solution:
Every mother is a woman → Mothers inside Women.
Some women are doctors and some mothers are doctors → Doctors overlap both.
Diagram (c) shows a small circle inside a big circle, and a third circle overlapping both.

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship between Dog, Animal and Cat?
questions.solution:
Dogs are animals and cats are animals → both inside Animal.
No dog is a cat → the two small circles are separate.
Diagram (d) shows this.

questions.q: Study the diagram. How many people are singers and dancers but NOT actors?
questions.solution:
Singers ∩ Dancers, outside Actors = the region marked 5.
(The 3 in the centre are also actors, so they are not counted.)

questions.q: Study the diagram. How many singers are also actors?
questions.solution:
Singers ∩ Actors = the region with 4 (singer and actor only) + the centre 3 (all three).
4 + 3 = 7.

questions.q: Which diagram best represents the relationship between Graduates, Teachers and Unemployed persons?
questions.solution:
Some teachers are graduates and some unemployed persons are graduates → Graduates overlaps both.
A teacher has a job, so no teacher is unemployed → Teachers and Unemployed are separate.
Diagram (b): a middle circle overlapping two circles that do not touch each other.

questions.q: Study the diagram. How many people belong to exactly two of the three groups?
questions.solution:
Exactly two groups = the three overlap regions that exclude the centre.
Singers–Dancers only: 5; Dancers–Actors only: 7; Singers–Actors only: 4.
5 + 7 + 4 = 16.

flashcards.back: Pairwise overlaps only, not the centre
